source: Three fresh-worker Chromium samples of packaged release WASM with explicit mobile browser safety budgets
notes: peakKiB is committed WebAssembly.Memory.buffer.byteLength high-water, not JavaScript heap usage.
maximumKiB is the shared-memory reservation limit supplied to WebAssembly.Memory; it can exceed committed high-water and is gated independently.
The captured worst peaks were boot of a 2000-row persisted store 87424 KiB (0 KiB spread), steady100 87744 KiB (0 KiB spread), and pull10k 91264 KiB (0 KiB spread).
The gate repeats those three fresh-worker scenarios and reports the worst run instead of averaging regressions away.
The 96/96/104 MiB committed ceilings and 512 MiB reservation ceiling are explicit project mobile-safety budgets, not inferred engine kill limits.
Chromium measures the real release artifact deterministically but is not a substitute for WebKit process limits; physical iPhone and iPad validation remains required.
